findings.evidence: Mathlib/Topology/Constructible.lean:251,256 has only `IsConstructible.preimage_of_isOpenEmbedding` and `preimage_of_isClosedEmbedding`; grep for a spectral-map version found nothing.
findings.fix: Factor it out as a public lemma, e.g. `IsSpectralMap.isConstructible_preimage` (or `IsConstructible.preimage_of_isSpectralMap`), and use it here.
findings.issue: The local `hpre` proves a general fact, that the preimage of a constructible set under a spectral map between spectral spaces is constructible, and hides it inside a proof.

findings.evidence: Both proofs repeat the same `let k/a/b` lines and the same `simp only [preimage_union, ← preimage_comp, ← coe_comp, c.w]` finish.
findings.fix: Add a private lemma: for `a : k ⟶ i`, `b : k ⟶ j`, `c.π.app i ⁻¹' V ∪ c.π.app j ⁻¹' W = c.π.app k ⁻¹' (F.map a ⁻¹' V ∪ F.map b ⁻¹' W)`, and use it in both inductions.
findings.issue: The step 'move two stage-wise preimages to the common stage `IsCofiltered.min i j` and rewrite the union with `c.w`' appears twice: lines 85-96 in `exists_compactOpen_preimage_of_isLimit` and lines 109-121 in `exists_constructible_preimage_of_isLimit`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib Profinite/Product.lean:98 defines `π := { app := fun J ↦ ConcreteCategory.ofHom (π_app C (· ∈ unop J)) }` and has no simp lemma for the cone's projection.
findings.fix: First prove `(c.π.app j ⟨x, _⟩).val = fun i : j.unop ↦ x i` as a named `have`, using `simp [Profinite.IndexFunctor.π_app]` or a comment explaining the defeq, then rewrite with it instead of relying on bare `rfl`.
findings.issue: `exact ⟨_, h, rfl⟩` and `Subtype.ext he` (line 61) only work because Lean unfolds `mapCone`/`indexCone`/`ConcreteCategory.ofHom`/`IndexFunctor.π_app` into coordinate restriction. Line 47 likewise uses `inferInstanceAs` through `Profinite.toTopCat`. The comment at line 58 says what the projection is but not why `rfl` holds.

summary: The descent proofs inline a reusable fact (constructible sets pull back along spectral maps) and repeat the same common-stage union step in both theorems. The Cantor example closes goals with undocumented definitional equalities through Profinite's cone wrappers.
